newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister promises multimedia aid.
newsitem.headline: French minister promises multimedia aid.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the government would take action to help the development of multimedia in France, but seemed to favour aid for creators rather than consumers.
Speaking at a meeting on new technologies organised by Alcatel Alsthom, the French telecommunications firm, on Monday, Strauss-Kahn said France was lagging behind in the multimedia revolution.
"But we also have plenty of creators, plenty of ideas and I think we can move forward," he said.
"We need to take measures which would make the route from scientific research to industrial innovation easier, and which would facilitate the birth of companies working in these areas," he said.
He said the penetration of multimedia computers is poor in the French market compared to other countries, but said there were other reasons for this besides price.
"I think it is more a cultural problem, a problem of education from school onwards, rather than only a problem of price.
"Prices are a factor, of course, but they are falling. If it was enough to arrange prices, we would have an instant solution. I think the problem is more complicated than that," he said.
French President Jacques Chirac recently sought a sharp cut in Value Added Tax charged on multimedia products, but the measure was found to contravene European Union regulations.
Strauss-Kahn said he would push forward "anything to do with the public sphere" for multimedia.

"In government I will make an effort to go in this direction. This is the case for fiscal aid to facilitate the creation of enterprises, for reorienting part of research, or the introduction of these technologies at school," he said. WEM/SLA
